# sakura_apprun_dedicated_active_version (Resource)

Manages the active version of an AppRun dedicated application.  Every change to the version configuration creates a new version and activates it; previous versions are kept.  The number of the active version is `version`.  Create and update wait until the previous version has left every node, not until the new one is running; raise `timeouts.update` for a large `fixed_scale`.

Unlike `sakura_apprun_dedicated_version`, this resource represents whichever version is active, so a version activated outside of Terraform is followed on refresh.  An apply whose plan predates such an activation is refused; the check is best effort and does not cover an activation during the apply itself.  Do not combine it with `sakura_apprun_dedicated_application.active_version` (both would activate versions) or `sakura_apprun_dedicated_version` (its version cannot be deleted while this resource keeps it active) on the same application.

Import with the application ID; the application must have an active version.  The first plan after an import may order `env_vars` and `secret_vars` differently; list them in the order of the state.  Destroying the resource, or removing it from the configuration, deactivates the application and waits until its containers have stopped; use `terraform state rm` to stop managing the active version without deactivating it.  After a deactivation outside of Terraform, the next apply creates a new version from the configuration, `image` included.

To deploy the image outside of Terraform (e.g. from a CI/CD pipeline), add `image` to `ignore_changes`; it must still be set for the first apply, and later versions are created with the image currently deployed:

```terraform
resource "sakura_apprun_dedicated_active_version" "main" {
  # ...
  lifecycle {
    ignore_changes = [image]
  }
}
```

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "sakura_apprun_dedicated_cluster" "main" {
  name = "ExampleCluster"
}

resource "sakura_apprun_dedicated_application" "main" {
  cluster_id = data.sakura_apprun_dedicated_cluster.main.id
  name       = "ExampleApplication"
}

resource "sakura_apprun_dedicated_active_version" "main" {
  application_id = sakura_apprun_dedicated_application.main.id
  cpu            = 1000
  memory         = 1024
  scaling_mode   = "manual"
  fixed_scale    = 1
  image          = "nginx:latest"

  exposed_ports = [
    {
      target_port = 80
    }
  ]
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `application_id` (String) The ID of the application.
- `cpu` (Number) The CPU limit in millicores (e.g., 1000 = 1 CPU). This must be in the range [`100`-`64000`]
- `image` (String) The container image, e.g. `nginx:latest`
- `memory` (Number) The memory limit in megabytes. This must be in the range [`128`-`131072`]
- `scaling_mode` (String) The scaling mode (manual, autoscale)

### Optional

> **NOTE**: [Write-only arguments](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments) are supported in Terraform 1.11 and later.

- `cmd` (List of String) application command line i.e. the command and arguments
- `env_vars` (Attributes List) Environment variables.  Use `secret_vars` for secrets (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--env_vars))
- `exposed_ports` (Attributes List) Ports that the application exposes (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--exposed_ports))
- `fixed_scale` (Number) Number of nodes when scaling mode is `manual`. This must be in the range [`1`-`50`]
- `max_scale` (Number) Maximum number of nodes when scaling mode is `autoscale`. This must be in the range [`1`-`50`]
- `min_scale` (Number) Minimum number of nodes when scaling mode is `autoscale`. This must be in the range [`1`-`50`]
- `registry_password` (String, [Write-only](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments)) Login password for the container registry.  A change of this value alone makes no plan; change it together with another attribute, e.g. `registry_password_action`
- `registry_password_action` (String) Password configuration method. This must be one of [`keep`/`remove`/`new`].  Note that `terraform import` cannot restore this field
- `registry_username` (String) Login user name for the container registry
- `scale_in_threshold` (Number) When to scale in when scaling mode is `autoscale`. This must be in the range [`30`-`70`]
- `scale_out_threshold` (Number) When to scale out when scaling mode is `autoscale`. This must be in the range [`50`-`99`]
- `secret_vars` (Attributes List) Secret environment variables.  Unlike `env_vars`, values are write-only and never land in the state.  `terraform import` puts every secret here; declare each as `{ key = "..." }` alone to adopt the imported version as is, and set `value_wo` only when a new version with a new value is wanted (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--secret_vars))
- `timeouts` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `active_node_count` (Number) The number of nodes running the active version
- `created_at` (String) The creation timestamp of the active version
- `id` (String) The ID of the application, the same as `application_id`
- `version` (Number) The number of the active version.  Increases whenever a new version is created

<a id="nestedatt--env_vars"></a>
### Nested Schema for `env_vars`

Required:

- `key` (String) Environment variable name

Optional:

- `secret` (Boolean, Deprecated) Whether the value is sensitive
- `value` (String) The value.  Use `secret_vars` for secrets.  Omitting this field with the deprecated `secret = true` retains the previous version's secret value


<a id="nestedatt--exposed_ports"></a>
### Nested Schema for `exposed_ports`

Required:

- `target_port` (Number) The port that the application listens to. This must be in the range [`1`-`65535`]

Optional:

- `health_check` (Attributes) Health check configuration (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--exposed_ports--health_check))
- `host` (Set of String) Target `Host:` header value (only applicable when `http` or `https`)
- `lb_port` (Number) The port that the load balancer listens to.  Explicitly set it to `null` when you want to disconnect from the load balancer. This must be in the range [`1`-`65535`]
- `use_lets_encrypt` (Boolean) Whether the load balancer uses Let's Encrypt (applicable only when `https`)

<a id="nestedatt--exposed_ports--health_check"></a>
### Nested Schema for `exposed_ports.health_check`

Required:

- `interval_seconds` (Number) Health check intervals in seconds. This must be in the range [`3`-`60`]
- `path` (String) Health check endpoint
- `timeout_seconds` (Number) Time out in seconds until the health check fails. This must be in the range [`1`-`60`]



<a id="nestedatt--secret_vars"></a>
### Nested Schema for `secret_vars`

Required:

- `key` (String) Environment variable name

Optional:

- `value_wo` (String, [Write-only](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments)) The value, write-only.  Omitting this field retains the previous version's secret value.  Must be set together with `value_wo_version`
- `value_wo_version` (Number) The version of the `value_wo` field.  This value must be greater than 0 when set.  Terraform cannot detect changes of write-only values, so increment this to create a new application version with the new `value_wo`.  Note that `terraform import` cannot restore this field


<a id="nestedatt--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).
- `delete` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Setting a timeout for a Delete operation is only applicable if changes are saved into state before the destroy operation occurs.
- `update` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).
